summary: Ming Chen works in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Chen served as a professor at Peking University, with posts attested in 2001 and 2013, and taught Alexander O. Hsu, Weilin Wu, and Jinchao Zhao.

Ming Mei works in Buddhist studies. Mei earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. Liu earned a BA from the University of Hong Kong and a PhD from UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as professor at Hong Kong (~1980–2012).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Taisho University in 1976. Nishimura held posts at Taisho University, the Sanko Cultural Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1960–1991) and served as President of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006).
Minoru Inaba is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Inaba held an academic post at Kyoto University, serving as professor in 2011 and attested there in 2022.

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, he served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1964 to 1993.

Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil. ~1879). He served as professor at Johns Hopkins University (1879–1899) and Harvard University (appointed 1899).
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979), Kishimoto served as a professor there (~1994–2007) and held a post at Ochanomizu University (~2007–2018).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Miranda Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She pursued her studies under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest and studied at the University of Calcutta, later holding professorships at the Sorbonne and the University of Chicago.

Mireille Helffer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post as Chargé de Recherche at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1968–1993) and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University in 1985.

Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. Her academic appointments include serving as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich and holding a post at the University of Tübingen (both attested 2026).

Miri Albahari is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary. Albahari held posts at the University of Western Australia and UNSW.

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She received her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at Zagreb, Ljubljana (PhD), and the International Faculty of Comparative Law. He taught at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School, where he became Sterling Professor emeritus.
